headline: Heard updates on Town Center Master Plan and High Meadows housing; approved July minutes 6-0 with one abstention.
summary: Members heard a Town Center Master Plan update from the town planner. The director reported on the High Meadows affordable housing project, the Leed Himmel building, and other business activity. Members approved the July 14, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Approved the July 14, 2026 meeting minutes with corrections, 6 yes, 0 no, 1 abstention.
Kept the 5:30 P.M. meeting time for 2027 meetings; no one objected.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Economic Development Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, September 8, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner K. Good at 5:31 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 The roll was called by the Clerk, and the following members were present: 
Present 
Commissioner Ken Good, Chair 
Commissioner Petra Gardella 
Commissioner Tammy Robinson 
Commissioner Anthony J. DelGrego 
Commissioner Howard K. Hill 
Commissioner Maggie Murolo 
Commissioner Romeo Ibanez 
 
Also in attendance were Steve Fontana, Economic Development Director; Eugene Livshits, 
Town Planner; Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk; and one 
member of the public, who attended virtually. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 8; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 0; Excused: 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
 
  1. Meeting Minutes for Tuesday, July 14th, 2026  
  Chairman K. Good requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Tuesday, July 14th, 
2026. 
 
Commissioner M. Maggie made the motion, and Commissioner T. Robinson 
seconded it. 
 
Present 
Commissioner K. Good, Chair 
Commissioner T. Robinson 
Commissioner A.J. DelGrego 
Commissioner H.K. Hill 
Commissioner M. Murolo
Commissioner R. Ibanez 
 
Abstentions 
Commissioner P. Gardella 
 
The previous meeting minutes with corrections. 
 
The motion passed. 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 6, No 0, Abstentions 1, Absent 0. 
  
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
You will have 3 minutes to speak and will be notified when you have 30 seconds 
remaining to avoid being muted at the completion of 3 minutes.   
 No members of the public offered comment. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Clerk B. Belton-Robinson reported that she reviewed the Commission’s email and had not 
received any new correspondence. Chairman K. Good stated that he had also reviewed his 
email and had not received any additional correspondence. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No executive session was held. 
7. CHAIRMAN'S REPORTS   
 
 
  1. Business Community Update  
  Chairman K. Good reported that approximately 74 new businesses registered in 
Hamden in July and 69 registered in August. Registrations included cleaning and 
building services, wholesalers, residential landlords, hospitality and food businesses, 
and a Jamaican mobile food business. 
 
Chairman K. Good stated that the continued registration of new businesses was 
encouraging and reflected ongoing small-business activity in Hamden. 
 
Chairman K. Good also noted that Walmart had begun its build-out/expansion in 
Hamden Plaza. 
 
Chairman K. Good discussed the announced closure of Leed Himmel Industries, a 
longstanding aluminum extrusion and fabrication manufacturer on Leeder Hill Drive 
whose history dates back to the early 1900s. He said that, based on information he 
reviewed, the closure was attributed to rising operating expenses, including employee
health insurance, workers’ compensation, electricity, property taxes, and higher raw-
material costs tied to federal tariffs. Chairman K. Good noted the significance of losing 
a longtime Hamden manufacturer and stated that Director S. Fontana could provide 
additional information during his report. 
  2. Hamden Small Business Academy  
  Chairman K. Good reported that the final cohort of the Hamden Small Business 
Academy, which had been funded through ARPA, concluded in August. 
 
The program was available to Hamden businesses and residents and provided 
training on starting and operating a small business. Chairman K. Good attended the 
final cohort’s pitch competition and participated in evaluating business ideas and 
providing feedback. 
 
Chairman K. Good stated that the program had been valuable and noted that Director 
S. Fontana had previously discussed identifying opportunities to continue or replace 
this type of small-business programming. 
  3. EDC Alliances  
  Chairman K. Good reported on developing relationships with local universities. 
 
Chairman K. Good and Commissioner R. Ibanez recently met with representatives 
from the University of New Haven, along with Commissioner Thomas Fortuna of the 
Finance Commission. The discussion focused on potential partnerships that could 
mutually benefit Hamden and the University. 
 
Potential areas of collaboration include: 
 
• Economic development analytics, research, and analysis to support planning 
and investment decisions; 
• Redevelopment analysis, including market research, benchmarking 
comparable communities, and evaluating potential uses for strategic 
properties; 
• Small-business and entrepreneurship initiatives to strengthen Hamden’s 
entrepreneurial ecosystem and connect businesses with resources; and 
• Talent retention and workforce strategies connecting local employers with 
university students and graduates. 
 
Chairman Good stated that Commissioner T. Fortuna initiated the conversation 
through his relationship with the University and that discussions would continue. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez said similar discussions were underway with Quinnipiac 
University. He emphasized identifying areas where the universities’ institutional 
priorities naturally intersect with Hamden’s economic development priorities and 
moving those relationships from dialogue to coordination and action. 
 
Chairman K. Good also discussed the difficulty municipalities have experienced 
recruiting employees with specialized municipal finance and accounting experience.
He stated that Commissioner T. Fortuna had discussed with the University of New 
Haven the possibility of educational programming designed to prepare accounting 
professionals specifically for municipal government. 
 
Commissioner T. Robinson stated that she has worked with the University of New 
Haven through youth initiatives and noted that the University offers valuable technical 
assistance to nonprofit organizations, including grant-reporting support and newer 
programming related to the use of artificial intelligence. She suggested that similar 
resources could potentially benefit Hamden businesses. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez suggested developing a centralized way to identify and 
publicize the various educational, technical-assistance, and business-development 
resources available to Hamden businesses and residents. 
  4. 2027 Economic Development Meeting Calendar  
  Chairman K.Good discussed the Commission’s 2027 meeting schedule and asked 
whether members wished to continue meeting at 5:30 P.M. 
 
No one objected to keeping the 5:30 P.M. meeting time. 
 
Chairman K. Good stated that he would finalize the 2027 meeting calendar and 
submit it to the Town Clerk’s Office before the applicable deadline. 
 
Chairman K. Good also suggested that the Commission consider holding at least one 
in-person meeting before the end of 2026, possibly during the holiday season. 
8. GUEST SPEAKER   
 
 
 1. Eugene Livshits, Hamden Town Planner 
• Town Center Master Plan 
 
       
  Chairman K. Good introduced Eugene Livshits, Hamden Town Planner, to provide an 
update on the Town Center Master Plan. 
 
Chairman K. Good clarified for the record that the agenda incorrectly listed the High 
Meadows Project under the guest speaker section. High Meadows would instead be 
addressed by Director S. Fontana during the Director’s Report. 
 
Mr. Livshits explained that the Town Center Master Plan originated as a collaborative 
initiative involving Planning and Zoning, Economic Development, Capital Projects and 
Grants, and Engineering. The Town successfully received planning funding through 
the Community Investment Fund (CIF) and is working with consultants SLR and 
Public Works Partners. 
 
The purpose of the project is to establish a long-term vision and roadmap for the 
growth and evolution of Hamden’s Town Center. 
 
The study area centers primarily on the Whitney Avenue/Dixwell Avenue intersection
and includes commercial, residential, recreational, and civic areas surrounding Town 
Center Park, Miller Memorial Library, Hamden Government Center, the Police and 
Fire Departments, and nearby businesses. 
 
Mr. Livshits stated that the plan is intended to create a stronger sense of place and a 
more cohesive downtown environment. The plan will evaluate strategies to: 
• Support smart development and economic vitality; 
• Strengthen local businesses; 
• Improve public spaces; 
• Improve pedestrian, bicycle, roadway, and transit connectivity; 
• Create a more walkable and pedestrian-friendly environment; 
• Identify redevelopment and infill opportunities; and 
• Review zoning regulations for potential barriers involving uses, building height, 
density, and other development standards. 
 
A market analysis has been completed. Mr. Livshits stated that the analysis identified 
opportunities in dining, apparel, entertainment, and recreation, while personal-service 
businesses were an existing strength. 
 
Mr. Livshits demonstrated the project’s online StoryMap and stated that the 
community survey remained open, with approximately 250 responses received at that 
time. The team previously held an in-person public workshop on July 22 at Thornton 
Wilder Hall, and a virtual workshop was also available. 
 
Additional engagement will include interviews and focus groups involving businesses, 
property owners, youth, seniors, and other stakeholders. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez asked about coordination with Quinnipiac University and 
potential alignment between the Town Center planning process, transit planning, and 
Quinnipiac’s transportation system. Mr. Livshits stated that the consultant team had 
reached out to Quinnipiac and that the University had previously expressed interest in 
participating. He agreed that coordination would be valuable. 
 
Mr. Livshits also discussed the relationship between the Town Center Master Plan 
and the planned Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) investment along Dixwell Avenue. The 
planning process is intended to leverage that transportation investment and examine 
potential connections to the Town Center area. 
 
Chairman Good asked how recommendations from the Master Plan would ultimately 
be implemented and funded. 
 
Mr. Livshits reported that the Town received approximately $250,000 in CIF planning 
funds. If future CIF funding remains available, the completed plan could position 
Hamden to seek implementation funding. 
 
The Master Plan will also help inform Hamden’s next Plan of Conservation and 
Development (POCD), which expires in 2029, and could lead to regulatory changes 
considered by the Planning and Zoning Commission. Future grant applications may
require Legislative Council approval. 
 
Chairman K. Good expressed interest in having the Economic Development 
Commission participate in the upcoming POCD process. Mr. Livshits stated that 
Economic Development Commission participation would be important because 
economic development is a major component of the comprehensive planning process. 
 
Discussion followed regarding the damaged clock structure and fountain in the Town 
Center area. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that the Chamber of Commerce originally installed the 
clock structure about 30 years ago. The Town and Chamber have discussed 
removing the damaged structure and replacing it with a simpler structure that could 
continue to advertise Town and Chamber events. 
 
Mr. Livshits stated that Engineering had previously studied options regarding the 
fountain and that relevant findings could be incorporated into the Master Plan. 
 
Commissioner P. Gardella asked whether housing would be actively considered as 
part of the Town Center Master Plan and cited several underutilized sites that could 
potentially accommodate housing. 
 
Mr. Livshits confirmed that housing will be part of the Town Center Master Plan and 
that opportunities for additional housing and redevelopment of underutilized properties 
will be examined. He noted, however, that development of privately owned property 
ultimately depends on the property owner. 
 
Commissioner T. Robinson suggested exploring whether the Graustein Memorial 
Fund, which has a presence in the Town Center area, might be interested in 
supporting smaller projects within the area. Mr. Livshits welcomed additional 
connections and stakeholder participation. 
 2. High Meadows Project 
• Town Center Master Plan 
• Economic Development Department Update 
 
       
  
 
9. DIRECTOR'S REPORT   
 Director S. Fontana thanked the Commission for its support of the Liuzzi tax incentive. He 
reported that the company had signed the necessary paperwork, begun its 
expansion/addition, and may pursue further expansion in the future. 
 
Leed Himmel Property 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that a growing Connecticut industrial/commercial company is 
expected to acquire the approximately 116,000-square-foot Leed Himmel building within 
the next several months.
The prospective company plans to renovate the facility and expand its operations. Director 
S. Fontana estimated that the relocation could initially involve several dozen jobs, 
potentially approximately 40–50 positions, with opportunities for additional growth over the 
next five to ten years. 
 
He stated that the company utilizes technologically advanced manufacturing processes 
and that additional information may become available in the November–December 
timeframe. 
 
1935 State Street 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that a small housing development is moving forward at 1935 
State Street, at State Street and Ridge Road near the DMV. 
 
The project has received Planning and Zoning approvals and is working on a tax-incentive 
application. Director S. Fontana stated that approximately 20% of the units are expected to 
be affordable at or below 80% of Area Median Income, with the remaining units market 
rate. 
 
Construction could begin in spring 2027. 
 
Cooper House Square 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that he and Town Planner Livshits met with the developers of 
Cooper House Square. 
 
The developers are close to signing a lease for the historic small red building at the front of 
the property for a retail use. 
 
Director S. Fontana also discussed the broader challenges affecting housing and mixed-
use development, including higher interest rates, tariffs affecting construction materials, 
uncertainty in material costs, and Hamden’s tax burden. He said these factors have made 
some projects that were previously feasible harder to finance. 
 
Retail and Business Activity 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that retail activity continues to move forward. 
 
A grand opening was held for Wonder in Hamden Plaza. 
 
A vintage/thrift store called The Mason Jar opened on Whitney Avenue in Mount Carmel. 
 
Director S. Fontana also reported that Ross Dress for Less was scheduled to open on 
October 10, 2026. 
 
Small Business and Entrepreneurship Programming 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that he met with Virginia Spell of the Urban League of 
Southern Connecticut regarding opportunities to continue entrepreneurial programming 
following the conclusion of the Hamden Small Business Academy.
The Urban League operates DNA of an Entrepreneur, a semiannual small-business 
academy. Director S. Fontana encouraged commissioners to refer interested Hamden 
residents and businesses to the program and stated that he hoped to establish an ongoing 
collaborative relationship with the Urban League. 
 
Director S. Fontana also discussed potential university partnerships. 
 
He stated that the University of New Haven has resources that could potentially connect 
faculty, students, and businesses to solve industrial and commercial business problems, 
including issues involving manufacturing processes, product development, packaging, and 
technology. 
 
He also identified opportunities to partner with Quinnipiac University on entrepreneurship 
programming, pitch competitions, technical assistance, mentorship, and other support for 
Hamden businesses. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez stated that Quinnipiac’s Center for Innovation and 
Entrepreneurship is already pursuing similar work. He noted that Dr. David Tomczyk’s 
small and family business entrepreneurship course pairs students with local businesses to 
solve real-world business problems and that the University is interested in increasing the 
number of Hamden businesses participating. 
 
Commissioner T. Robinson emphasized that business-development resources should also 
support established businesses seeking to grow, not solely startups. 
 
Director S. Fontana agreed and noted that the Urban League also offers accelerator 
programming for established businesses. 
 
Workforce Development 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that he and the Mayor attended the 80th anniversary 
celebration of Porter and Chester Institute. He highlighted the institution’s Dixwell Avenue 
facility and workforce-training programs, including automotive, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, 
and nursing programs. 
 
Walmart Expansion 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that Walmart’s Hamden expansion appeared primarily intended 
to strengthen its ability to compete with supermarkets and larger retailers such as Aldi, 
Stop & Shop, and ShopRite rather than specifically targeting small independent retailers. 
 
Hamden 2040 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that he, Town Planner Livshits, Stephen White, and Councilor 
Abdul Osmanu were developing an initiative tentatively called “Hamden 2040: Building 
Toward Hamden’s Future.” 
 
The initiative is intended to create an ongoing conversation among residents, businesses, 
and Town officials regarding Hamden’s long-term direction.
An in-person community event was being considered for the fall, potentially in October. 
The format would emphasize short introductory remarks followed by informal conversations 
and interactive opportunities for residents to provide ideas and feedback. 
 
Industrial Expansion Assistance Program 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that he was developing a proposed Industrial Expansion 
Assistance Program. 
 
The pilot program would provide small grants to growing businesses seeking to relocate to 
or expand in Hamden. Eligible expenses could include infrastructure and development 
costs such as water and sewer connections, architects, engineers, and similar site-
development expenses. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that he was considering repurposing approximately $45,000–
$60,000 from an existing departmental budget line to fund the pilot. 
 
Assistance would be capped at a fixed amount or approximately 50% of eligible project 
costs, whichever is less, and awards would be tied to commitments to create permanent 
full-time jobs. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that a final proposal would be shared with the Commission after 
additional review. 
 
Town Financial Audits 
 
Chairman K. Good asked whether Hamden’s outstanding financial audits affect 
businesses’ willingness to invest in the Town. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that they may affect perceptions of Hamden and also have a 
more direct financial impact. He reported that the Town remained unable to access the 
bond market for capital borrowing until the outstanding audits were completed. 
 
He stated that financial stability, predictable taxes, and the ability to borrow for capital 
projects would be important to Hamden’s economic development efforts. 
 1. High Meadows Project 
       
  Director S. Fontana reported that he and Town Planner Livshits recently participated 
in a productive meeting with the High Meadows developer and the Connecticut 
Department of Housing. 
 
The developer remains committed to Hamden and the project but continues working 
to assemble the financing necessary to complete the development. 
 
Director S. Fontana explained that because the approximately 150-unit project is 
planned as 100% affordable housing, it requires substantial public subsidy and does 
not have market-rate units available to cross-subsidize affordable units. 
 
The Town continues to assist the developer by providing information, connecting the
developer with resources and decision-makers, and supporting efforts to assemble 
the financing package. 
 
The anticipated timeline discussed included completion of the current financial 
planning work during fall 2026, due diligence and movement toward community 
engagement and land-use approvals in 2027, and financing efforts in 2028. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that he remained optimistic about the project while 
acknowledging that the process would take time because of the complexity of the 
financing. 
 2. Town Center Master Plan 
       
  
 
 3. Economic Development Department Update 
       
  Director S. Fontana provided an additional update regarding economic development 
opportunities along the Dixwell Avenue corridor. 
 
He stated that the Town is pursuing several long-term initiatives in southern Hamden, 
including Dixwell Connections, a proposed bicycle and pedestrian connection to the 
Farmington Canal Trail for which the Town intends to seek CIF funding. 
 
Director S. Fontana identified the former Kramer Iron site on Morse Street, near the 
trail, as a potential redevelopment opportunity. The site consists of approximately 
seven parcels totaling roughly two acres. 
 
Because the property owes significant taxes to the Town, Director S. Fontana stated 
that the Town is permitted to conduct an environmental assessment. He contracted 
with BL Companies to perform a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment at an 
estimated cost of approximately $3,000. 
 
The assessment will help determine whether environmental conditions make 
acquisition through tax foreclosure feasible. 
 
If the site is suitable, Director S. Fontana stated that the Town could potentially 
acquire it, seek state and federal funding for demolition and remediation, and prepare 
it for future mixed-use redevelopment. 
 
He expected to have additional information by the October or November Commission 
meeting. 
10. OLD BUSINESS   
 There was no old business. 
11. NEW BUSINESS   
 There was no new business. 
 
Chairman Good announced several upcoming Chamber of Commerce events, including a 
Business After Hours event at Quinnipiac University, the Chamber’s Cars and Commerce 
event at Town Center Park, and an upcoming Business Before Hours event involving
candidates representing legislative districts that include Hamden. 
 
Chairman Good stated that he would forward the event information to commissioners. The 
Clerk stated that the materials could also be included with the agenda packet. 
12. ADJOURNMENT   
 Commissioner Petra Gardella made a motion to adjourn. Commissioner Romeo Ibanez 
seconded the motion. 
 
The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:25 P.M.
